runs.text: Know the risk. Learn from the past. Prepare for the future.

Good morning. We are Team EUREKA. ClimateGuard AI is an India-focused web-based application for climate-risk awareness, geographic hazard exploration and preparedness learning. We also demonstrate source-backed monitoring and a simulated response workflow. Source: supplied ClimateGuard_AI_Resilience_Blueprint.pptx, slides 14–18. These slides describe a concept, not proof of validated operational performance.
Users need to understand which hazards affect a location, why it is vulnerable, and how to prepare.
Official alerts already exist. We explore the connection to local understanding and training.
Source: CEEW (20 May 2025). District share and population share use different denominators.

The problem is connecting a hazard warning to local context: what affects this location, why it is vulnerable, and how to prepare. Intended early users are students, educators, residents and community volunteers. Official warning services already exist; SACHET provides geo-targeted alerts. Our integration and learning gap is a design hypothesis, not a measured market gap. CEEW's 2025 study assessed 734 districts: about 57% were high or very high heat risk and those districts housed 76% of India's population. These are different denominators and are not counts of our users. 43% is the rounded complement. Sources: https://www.ceew.in/publications/mapping-climate-risks-and-impacts-of-extreme-heatwave-disaster-in-indian-districts; https://sachet.ndma.gov.in/ . Canva chart design: https://canva.link/cbyvxudo1ymblax. The native PowerPoint chart preserves exact rounded data and proportional scaling.
One place to explore local hazards and learn how to prepare
Combines geographic context, educational profiles and visible data sources.
Prototype scope: five detailed profiles; demonstration scores; no disaster prediction.

ClimateGuard AI brings location-based climate education, source-labelled hazard information and preparedness guidance into one application. The concept flow is adapted from the supplied slides 14–18. Some educational screens still contain demonstration content. The benefit of better understanding is intended and must be validated with users. Diagram authored in FigJam: https://www.figma.com/board/4XSE3ihyhkTNFJNg2Ty6BW; recreated here as editable native nodes and connectors. Source: supplied ClimateGuard_AI_Resilience_Blueprint.pptx, slides 14–18. These slides describe a concept, not proof of validated operational performance.
Backend: Node.js + Vite 8 middleware · No persistent database
Input: location + feeds + reports     Process: normalization + rules     Output: map + learning + demo status

Input: selected location, static profiles, external hazard responses, and demo incident reports. Processing: Node.js middleware inside the Vite development server normalizes XML/GeoJSON/CSV, caches feeds and assigns coordinates to states with point-in-polygon logic. A finite-state workflow constrains incident actions. Output: React screens and Cesium map markers. Static profiles are bundled with the frontend. Incidents and audit entries are in memory; there is no persistent database. The optional chatbot uses a configured external LLM API; no disaster-prediction model is trained. The AI does not dispatch teams or independently verify current hazards. Source: vite.config.js; server/hazards.js; server/incidents.js; server/chat.js; src/components/IndiaGlobe.jsx. Main active map engine is CesiumJS.
Contribution: local learning with transparent data and workflow practice
Connect a selected place to hazards, vulnerability context and preparedness.
Keep source and timestamp visible. Distinguish unavailable data from no events.
Demonstrate review, verification, assignment and resolution with activity history.
Supports awareness and training. Official warnings and emergency decisions stay with authorities.

The contribution is an integrated educational workflow, rather than a claim that disaster platforms did not previously exist. SACHET already aggregates official warnings. Our prototype combines local learning, map exploration, source freshness and simulated report handling. We have not established global novelty, validated scoring, superior alert accuracy, or measured improvement over existing services. All dashboard risk scores must be described as demonstration values. Source: supplied slides 14–18; README.md; docs/LIVE_OPERATIONS.md; https://sachet.ndma.gov.in/ .
Public hazard services; keys where required. Optional LLM calls may incur charges.
Production backend, authentication, durable storage and load testing.
Minutes · shorter bars refresh the cache sooner
Implementation settings, not guaranteed warning latency.

A classroom demonstration runs on a laptop with Node.js, browser and internet. React, Vite and CesiumJS provide the application foundation. Public data services may have terms, quotas or key requirements; FIRMS requires a key and chatbot use may incur provider charges. Free or low-cost access does not imply unlimited production usage. Cache intervals reduce repeat requests: USGS 1 min, official alerts 2 min, Open-Meteo 5 min, FIRMS 15 min. They are not end-to-end warning latency guarantees. Public scaling requires a separate production backend, authentication, persistent storage, quotas and monitoring. No load testing is claimed. Source: package.json; server/hazards.js; docs/LIVE_OPERATIONS.md; docs/CHATBOT_SETUP.md. Canva chart design: https://canva.link/cbyvxudo1ymblax; native chart recreated for exact proportional data.
Students and residents: clearer risk understanding.
Pilot measures: source-finding time, knowledge gain and workflow completion.
Impact is not yet measured. No claims of lives saved, cost reduction or prediction accuracy.

Expected benefits: clearer local risk understanding for students and residents; structured practice for community volunteers; a basis for feedback from educators and domain reviewers. These benefits have not been measured in a field study. Current software evidence: five bundled location profiles, four integrated hazard/feed families and 19 passing automated tests reported in the repository review on 8 October 2026, with mocked providers and simulated incidents. Tests do not establish scientific accuracy or real-world safety. Proposed pilot: compare time to locate a relevant source, a short before/after knowledge quiz, and completion of a simulated incident lifecycle. Collect baseline values before estimating improvements. Source: supplied ClimateGuard_AI_Resilience_Blueprint.pptx, slides 14–18. These slides describe a concept, not proof of validated operational performance. Source: locationsData.js; hazards.js; npm test results from project review.
Archived prototype screenshot · 14 September 2026 · response actions are simulated

Demonstrate the application locally with npm run dev at http://localhost:5173. The launcher also starts the adapted God's Eye View runtime on localhost:4173. Follow one story: select Kolkata, inspect source and timestamp, create a clearly labelled demo report, review it, assign a demo team, resolve it and inspect the activity history. Do not claim this is deployed publicly. The image is an existing repository verification screenshot dated 14 September 2026, not today's live feed. It shows the embedded Live View integration and simulation banner. Source image: artifacts/live-view-redesign.png, described in artifacts/README.md.
